criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the load-bearing execution paths and step-to-step write behavior. The visual-render path is incorrect as written because it calls removed Gamma tooling (lines 275-296, especially line 285), and the Prepared Questions write target points to Step 5 instead of Step 6 (line 575). Those are functional defects in core workflow instructions, not cosmetic nits.

The skill is broad and most required sections are present, but I checked obvious edge cases and found an unresolved one: the roundup carousel is mandatory, limited to 3-5 slides, and also specified as one slide per event (line 233), while the roundup model can cover more than five events. That leaves a real but secondary gap.

I checked house conventions I could verify from the artifact itself: frontmatter/path naming are fine, but source-of-truth discipline is not. Step 7 embeds stale execution behavior ('Canva MCP') that contradicts Step 3b.5 and should have been deferred to the canonical visual-briefs spec instead (line 508).

I specifically checked for resurrected tombstoned decisions/tools. The skill makes Gamma the default generator for all visuals (line 277) and operationalizes that in Step 3b.5, which the supplied tombstone check identifies as a removed path. That's a direct anti-pattern under this rubric.

I reviewed maintainability and honesty of explanatory text against actual behavior. The artifact has multiple stale/internal contradictions: Step 6 claims Step 4 now produces one best note per person (line 471), but the procedure still requires A/B variants; the error-handling note at line 607 misidentifies Step 5 as DM generation. Failures are not opaque, but the guidance is not reliably self-consistent.
